column1: # ZAP baseline alerts we have decided about. Everything else fails the build.
# IGNORE is a decision, not a mute button. Every line here has to say why the
# alert is not worth acting on, or which issue is acting on it — an entry that
# says neither is how a scan turns into a formality. The rule ids are ZAP's:
# apps/web/src/lib/security-headers.ts, which are why this file is as short as it
# is. Four of the eleven alerts in the first run were fixed rather than listed —
# nosniff on /favicon.svg and /robots.txt, a Permissions-Policy on the built
# assets, CORP and COOP everywhere, and a year of caching on the hashed bundles
# that were being revalidated on every navigation. The alternative to fixing an
# alert is not always ignoring it.

column3: CSP on the document surface needs a nonce for the SSR hydration script — #134. The api sends default-src 'none'; the dashboard sends none yet, and a wrong script-src breaks hydration silently.

One rule id for three headers. CORP and COOP ARE sent, on every response, and are asserted by unit tests in both apps — this covers only Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy, which is deliberately absent: require-corp buys cross-origin isolation (SharedArrayBuffer, precise timers) that this app does not want, and costs every cross-origin subresource having to opt in, so the first external avatar or font anyone adds would break silently.

/reset-password?token. A reset token in a URL is how an emailed reset link works — every implementation of one. It is single-use, expires, and Referrer-Policy keeps the path off cross-origin requests. Removing it means moving to a code the user retypes, which is a product decision and not a header.

Private IP Disclosure on /assets/index-*.js. The match is the literal "10.0.0.0/8" inside the TRUST_PROXY validation message in apps/web/src/lib/env.ts, which is documentation of the expected format, not an address of any deployment. Verified in the built bundle.
